raw_plan.interpretation: Treat this as a one-email acquisition introduction for a new IT buyer whose current use of Scribe is unknown. The email will present one bounded product use—turning a browser-based IT procedure into a how-to guide—and ask the reader to try that procedure on the free Basic plan.

intent.desired_action: Sign up for the free Basic plan and generate a how-to guide for one browser-based IT procedure.

raw_plan.reader: IT managers and system administrators responsible for internal support documentation, without assuming their procedures are currently undocumented or that they use another documentation product.
raw_plan.reader_scope: The supported use is narrow: a buyer can use free Basic in a browser to generate a how-to guide for one IT procedure. Desktop application capture requires Pro or Enterprise. Treat procedures living as tribal knowledge as a conditional situation, not a fact about every recipient.
raw_plan.promise: If an IT procedure currently lives in someone's head, Scribe gives the team a concrete way to turn the work into a browser-based how-to guide and try that use for free.
raw_plan.orientation: Scribe is documentation and workflow-capture software that turns actions taken in applications into step-by-step how-to guides an IT team can share.
raw_plan.arc: In one email, move the reader from seeing process documentation as a separate writing task to seeing one real browser procedure as something they can turn into a guide with Scribe and evaluate for free.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: A single-email introduction must establish the useful operation, explain the automatic capture mechanism, and remove the immediate budget barrier in one pass. It does not assume an installed alternative or spend the email on pricing, compliance, customer results, or a broader rollout. The desktop boundary is included only to keep the free test accurate.

emails.selection_reason: This is the strongest supported first-use proposition for an IT buyer: it applies Scribe's documented capture mechanism to one concrete documentation task and gives the reader a free, browser-based way to judge the output without requiring procurement.

value_case.reader_benefit: If an IT procedure is currently carried in one person's head, the team can turn that performed work into a step-by-step guide instead of leaving the procedure undocumented.
value_case.mechanism: Scribe's Autocapture turns work already performed into Scribes automatically, while the free Basic plan supports generating how-to guides in the browser.
decision_conditions: The free Basic use described here is browser-based.
Capturing processes in desktop applications requires Pro or Enterprise.

claim_conditions: Frame tribal knowledge as a conditional situation; P1 is based on a single historical source and does not establish that every recipient has this problem.
Do not imply that desktop capture is included in Basic.
Do not state that Autocapture itself is a Basic-plan entitlement; the evidence establishes the capability and separately establishes free browser-based guide generation.
emails.target_audience: IT managers and system administrators responsible for internal support documentation
emails.job: Make a new IT buyer want to use Scribe for one real procedure and click to try browser-based guide generation for free.
emails.single_idea: Take one browser-based IT procedure your team may currently carry in memory and turn it into a how-to guide with Scribe; the Basic plan lets you try browser guide generation for free.
emails.felt_need: If an important procedure still lives as tribal knowledge, the team needs a practical way to turn it into documentation.
emails.mechanism: Scribe's Autocapture turns work already performed into Scribes automatically. For the first test, Basic lets the reader generate a how-to guide in the browser at no cost; desktop application capture is reserved for Pro and Enterprise.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: This is a credible alternative when an IT buyer's first concern is exposing sensitive information during workflow capture: it leads with the documented redaction mechanism and sends the reader to public IT documentation before asking them to create an account.

value_case.reader_benefit: For workflows that may expose sensitive fields, an IT team can consider a capture product with automatic redaction and workspace-level access controls.
value_case.mechanism: Scribe automatically redacts 150 categories of PII, PHI, and PCI and provides fine-grained workspace permissions.
decision_conditions: These are product-level security and redaction claims; the supplied evidence does not establish that they are included on the free Basic plan.
The documentation does not establish suitability for every organization's policies, systems, or jurisdiction.

claim_conditions: Use compliance language only as Scribe's documented posture, not as a blanket legal conclusion for the recipient or its clients.
Do not imply that automatic redaction removes the need for the reader's own security review.
alternative_arguments.single_idea: If sensitive information is a concern when capturing IT workflows, Scribe documents automatic redaction across 150 categories of PII, PHI, and PCI, plus fine-grained workspace permissions.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: During capture, Scribe automatically redacts the documented sensitive-data categories; workspace permissions provide controls over access to the resulting material.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: capturing an IT workflow may appear to require accepting unknown exposure of sensitive fields. After: the reader knows Scribe documents automatic redaction and permissions that are concrete enough to inspect before a formal evaluation.
must_not_say: That Scribe creates a blanket exemption from consent, contracts, regulation, or the reader's internal policies.
That compliance claims establish legal suitability for every recipient, client, or jurisdiction.
That every sensitive value will always be detected or redacted.
That these controls are included on Basic.
Any claim of time saved, fewer mistakes, zero risk, or superior protection versus competitors.
alternative_arguments.objection: Can we inspect the relevant redaction and access-control claims before creating an account?
alternative_arguments.call_to_action: Review Scribe's IT security and redaction details.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether Scribe's documented redaction and permission controls justify a formal product evaluation for the team's workflows.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The public IT page lets the reader inspect Scribe's stated automatic-redaction scope, compliance posture, and workspace permissions without first creating an account.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The page documents product claims; it does not validate organization-specific configuration, plan availability, legal applicability, or performance in the reader's environment.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Lead with the concrete redaction scope relevant to workflow capture, without using regulatory fear or implying that the recipient has already experienced a data-exposure incident.
